name: National Public Data (breached in 2024)
tip: The people-search site behind the 2024 breach that leaked Social Security numbers is back online. Keep the opt-out page open. Search your name, city and state on nationalpublicdata.com, open your card with View Full Profile and copy that page's link. Paste it into Your Profile Link on the opt-out page and tap Request Removal. Check it is you, enter your email and tap Confirm Removal. Then tap the green Remove button in the email from support@nationalpublicdata.com. If nothing there is you, tap NOT LISTED.

name: People Background Check
tip: Search your name and open your listing. Tap the gear icon next to your name, then Control Information. Enter your name and email, do the CAPTCHA, then tap the link they email you. They say it is gone within 48 hours. If nothing there is you, tap NOT LISTED.

name: TruthViewer
tip: Same company as WeInform and TruthRecord, but it needs its own request. Pick Remove My Information at the top, not the first option. Enter your name, birth date, city, ZIP and state, then your email, and tap Submit removal request. Do the robot check if one shows, then tap the link they email you: nothing is removed until you do. You cannot see whether you are listed without paying, so send the removal anyway. If a box asks for a credit card, that is their paid search, not the removal: close it.

You can also do it by phone at (833) 714-0641.

name: Thomson Reuters CLEAR (records database used by police)
tip: CLEAR is the records database that police, investigators and debt collectors search. This form opts you out of its sale and sharing: choose the do not sell or share option and fill in your details. They keep government records such as court and property records, and remove whole records only for judges, police, people at risk of harm and identity theft victims. If they ask for a copy of your ID, use THEY WANT ID.

name: PrivateEye (sister site of PeopleFinders)
tip: PrivateEye gets its records from PeopleFinders, so your PeopleFinders opt-out should clear it too. If you still find yourself here a few days after that, use this page: they email you a link to the removal form. If nothing there is you, tap NOT LISTED.

name: OpenDataUSA
tip: Shows names and addresses, and political donations too. Find your listing, then on this page enter a regular email address such as Yahoo or Gmail and send it. Tap the confirm and remove link in the email they send. If nothing there is you, tap NOT LISTED.

name: Unite 4 Heritage (people directory)
tip: Another people directory hiding on a borrowed website, like Men Stopping Violence. Find your listing, enter your email on this page and send it, then tap the button in the email they send. If nothing there is you, tap NOT LISTED.

name: H-E-B (shopping data for ads)
tip: H-E-B uses your shopping data for targeted ads with partners such as Google and Facebook. On this form choose Texas and ask to opt out of targeted advertising and the sale of your data. Use the email and phone on your H-E-B account so they can find you. Ask for deletion only if you do not mind losing your account history. You can also call 1-866-421-5608. No H-E-B account? Tap NOT LISTED.

name: Dollar General (shopping data for ads)
tip: Dollar General runs an ad network built on shopper data. Choose Texas and ask to opt out of sale, sharing and targeted ads. Your name, email and phone must match your Dollar General account, so use those, then tap the link they email you. You can also call 1-800-678-9258. No Dollar General account or app? Tap NOT LISTED.

name: Facebook: ads from your outside activity off
tip: Do this in the Facebook app. Tap the menu at the top left, then Settings and privacy, Settings, Accounts Center, Ad preferences, Manage info, then Activity from other businesses. Choose Don't allow us to use this activity to show you relevant ads and confirm. Then tap MARK AS DONE. No Facebook? Tap NOT LISTED.
